messages:
zoe (sales): Marlow is greenlit for a 2-week POC. Their security team wants a hosted API key flow that supports automated rotation from their k8s CI, and they asked if we support federated/OIDC exchanges instead of long-lived secrets. Can we confirm patterns and a minimal runbook?

dmitri (solutions): Two supported patterns for POCs: 1) Ephemeral hosted keys via our provisioning API (one-time client_secret) and a rotation job on their side. 2) OIDC token exchange: customer obtains an ID token from their IdP and calls our /v1/tokens/exchange to get a short-lived session token. For POCs we usually recommend ephemeral hosted keys (simpler) but we support both.

dmitri (solutions): Provisioning example (ephemeral key):
```
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/provision/keys
Authorization: Bearer <PROVISION_TOKEN>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "customer": "marlow",
  "type": "ephemeral",
  "ttl_seconds": 259200,    
  "scopes": ["generation:invoke"],
  "ip_allowlist": ["198.51.100.0/22"]
}
# returns {"key_id":"k_...","client_secret":"s_..."} (client_secret shown once)
```

dmitri (solutions): OIDC exchange example (recommended for zero-secret approach):
```
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tokens/exchange
Authorization: Bearer <PROVISION_TOKEN>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "idp": "https://accounts.example-idp.com/",
  "id_token": "<customer-id-token>",
  "audience": "redwood-poc",
  "scopes": ["generation:invoke"]
}
# returns {"session_token":"t_...","expires_at":"2026-03-22T10:00:00Z"}
```

anne (security): Security notes: for federated exchanges we require a pre-registered OIDC client and JWKS verification. Federated session tokens must be short (<= 1h). Ephemeral hosted keys for POCs can be approved up to 72h TTL with signoff. All issuance and revocations are logged to our audit trail and KMS. Revocation endpoint (admin): DELETE /v1/keys/{key_id}. For federated sessions we also record the id_token thumbprint so we can blacklist sessions if needed.

marlow (customer): Great. Our plan: a Kubernetes controller (CI) will run a rotation job to request a new secret, write to k8s Secret via CSI or api, and then trigger a rolling restart. Questions: 1) any gotchas with the one-time client_secret visibility? 2) what's our issuance rate limit? 3) can we request the session token instead (OIDC)?

dmitri (solutions): 1) client_secret is returned only once; ensure your controller captures it immediately and writes it to a vault/secret. 2) default issuance cap is 10 keys/hr per org; we can increase for automation testing — open a quick ticket. 3) yes, if you wire OIDC we can issue session tokens instead (preferred for no-secret workflows).

dmitri (solutions): Recommended k8s flow (copy/paste):
```bash
# create new key (in controller)
curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/provision/keys" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PROVISION_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"customer":"marlow","type":"ephemeral","ttl_seconds":259200}' \
  | jq -r '.client_secret' > /tmp/new_secret && \
# update k8s secret (example)
kubectl create secret generic redwood-api --from-file=secret=/tmp/new_secret -o yaml --dry-run=client | kubectl apply -f - && \
# rollout the deployment or use a sidecar to hot-swap
kubectl rollout restart deploy/my-service
```

keys-bot: Policy check: require audit_tag=poc:marlow on issuance; approver=anne. Issuance_limit=10/hr applied.

anne (security): Approved: 72h TTL for ephemeral keys for this POC (signed off). If Marlow uses OIDC exchange, session tokens must be <=1h. Callbacks (if used) must be HTTPS and validated by HMAC. Audit retention enabled for POC. Also: disable long-lived org API tokens for the org during the POC to reduce risk.

marlow (customer): Thanks 49c (heart), we'll start with OIDC exchange in staging and fall back to ephemeral keys if we hit trouble. Can you raise the issuance cap to 30/hr for our org while we run automation?

dmitri (solutions): Yes — I will open the ops request to bump to 30/hr for the POC window. Also sending a short runbook to you after provisioning.

zoe (sales): Action items: dmitri -> request issuance bump and provision initial token if Marlow wants it; anne -> confirm audit_tag and disable long-lived tokens; marlow -> wire OIDC client and send IdP metadata. I'll send the runbook with both OIDC and ephemeral options. :thumbsup:
